root_cause.text: The `mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()` function failed to disable vPort RX steering in the firmware before destroying RX work queue objects, leaving stale hardware configuration that routed incoming traffic completions to invalid or reused Completion Queues (CQs).
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states that `mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss()` "destroys the RX WQ objects but does not disable vPort RX steering in firmware," and the patch fixes this by adding a call to `mana_disable_vport_rx(mpc)` at the start of the destroy function to ensure the firmware stops routing traffic to the destroyed queues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Disable vPort RX steering before destroying RX WQ objects to prevent bogus completions on reused CQ IDs.
intent_record.what: Added a call to mana_disable_vport_rx(mpc) before destroying RX WQ objects in mana_ib_destroy_qp_rss(), along with explanatory comments.
intent_record.how: Prevents firmware from routing traffic to destroyed queues, avoiding bogus completions on reused CQ IDs when new queues are created later in mana_open().

intent_record.intent_summary: Corrects the queue deallocation sequence by updating RX disable logic and adding receive queue fencing to prevent teardown races.
intent_record.what: Replaced the mana_config_rss call with mana_disable_vport_rx and inserted a mana_fence_rqs call before mana_destroy_vport.
intent_record.how: Ensures receive queues are properly synchronized and the vPort RX is correctly disabled before resource cleanup, preventing race conditions during device deallocation.
